title: NAS 410 Audit Documentation for San Diego Suppliers
description: NAS 410 and Nadcap audit documentation for San Diego unmanned-systems, naval aviation and defense suppliers, for your Level 3 to approve. Contact Atlantis.
h1: NAS 410 and Nadcap AC7114 Audit Documentation for San Diego Unmanned Systems, Naval Aviation and Defense Suppliers
html:
San Diego builds unmanned aircraft, overhauls naval fighters and supports a defense supply chain in which composite structure, controlled technical data and tight customer oversight are normal. If your company runs an NDT process for that work and expects a Nadcap AC7114 audit or a prime's source audit, Atlantis NDT can prepare and review the NAS 410 documentation behind it, for approval by your own Responsible Level 3. Share your audit date and methods and we reply within one business day.

First, what Atlantis will and will not sign

Quality managers sometimes assume a Level III consultant can take the program off their hands. Under NAS 410 that is not how it works, and it is not what we offer. Atlantis is not, and does not act as, your Responsible Level 3. We do not certify anyone to NAS 410, and we deliver no NAS 410 training or examinations. Your company is the certifying employer, acting through the written practice it controls, and the Level 3 it designated in writing approves procedures, technique sheets, examinations and the written practice itself.

Our contribution is ASNT NDT Level III consulting focused on documentation and readiness: we read what you have against NAS 410, AC7114 and your customers' specifications, draft what is missing in your format, rebuild records that will not survive sampling, and rehearse the audit with your team. Atlantis holds Level III in ultrasonic, radiographic, magnetic particle, penetrant and visual testing, and no other methods; for any other method, the technical approval belongs to a Level 3 certified in it. Atlantis does not perform radiography in the United States, so radiographic work is limited to Level III review of procedures and records.

San Diego's aerospace base: unmanned aircraft, naval aviation and the suppliers between

Unmanned aircraft define much of the county's aerospace identity. Northrop Grumman runs its Unmanned Systems Center of Excellence in Rancho Bernardo, where work on the Global Hawk family, including the Navy's MQ-4C Triton and the NATO Alliance Ground Surveillance variant, has been consolidated. General Atomics Aeronautical Systems is based in Poway, and General Atomics lists several thousand employees across Poway, Rancho Bernardo, Torrey Pines and Sabre Springs. San Diego-based Cubic Corporation has appeared as a subcontractor on Northrop Grumman's MQ-8C Fire Scout helicopter program.

Naval aviation is the other anchor. Fleet Readiness Center Southwest at Naval Air Station North Island overhauls, repairs and modifies Navy and Marine Corps front-line aircraft and components, is the lead facility for F/A-18 Hornet and Super Hornet depot work, replaces aircraft center sections to extend service life, and produces metal and composite components. Around the base and the primes sits a subtier of machinists, composite fabricators, coating and plating houses, test labs and electronics manufacturers, many of them small and many of them working under defense contracts.

That mix produces NDT programs heavy in ultrasonic inspection of composite structure, penetrant and magnetic particle on machined metallic details, and eddy current on aluminum structure, run by companies whose customers are prime contractors or the government rather than airlines.

Audits a San Diego supplier can expect

AuditWho runs itWhat it wants from the NDT program
Nadcap NDTAn auditor contracted by the Performance Review Institute, using AC7114 and the method slash sheetsWritten practice compliance with NAS 410, personnel files, examinations, procedures, process control, observed jobs
Prime source or surveillance auditThe customer's supplier quality or special process teamCompliance with the prime's own NDT specifications and flow-downs, often deeper than Nadcap on technique approval
AS9100 registrar auditYour certification bodyControl of special processes, training and competence records, calibration, document control
Government quality oversightGovernment representatives under the contract's quality clausesEvidence that contract requirements, including any invoked personnel standard, are met and recorded
Upstream customer audit of you as a subcontractorA tier-one supplier that buys your NDT or your NDT-inspected partsYour certifications, approvals and how their purchase order requirements reach your floor

Each of these samples the same personnel files and procedures from a different angle, so a gap tends to surface eventually even if the first audit misses it. The guide to what Nadcap accreditation checks describes the Nadcap angle, and Nadcap AC7114 audit readiness covers preparation.

Composite airframes and bonded structure

Unmanned aircraft rely heavily on composite skins, spars and bonded assemblies, and so do many of the components a depot replaces. Ultrasonic inspection of these parts, whether pulse-echo by hand, through-transmission in a squirter system or automated scanning, is where San Diego technique files are thickest and where auditors spend the most time. They want to see how each technique was developed, what reference standard it uses, how gain and gates were set against that standard, what scan index and coverage the part requires, how indications are sized and recorded, and who approved the result.

Two record problems recur. The first is the approved technique that no longer matches the scanning program actually loaded on the machine, because someone adjusted a parameter and never revised the sheet. The second is a family of near-identical techniques for similar parts with no record of which part numbers each covers. We reconcile techniques with the equipment setups in use, consolidate where the customer specification allows, and prepare revised sheets for your ultrasonic Level 3 to approve. The aerospace UT compliance page lists the requirements that drive these files.

Metallic structure brings its own files. Depot-related and repair work on aluminum airframe structure leans on eddy current for cracks around fastener holes and for corrosion under paint, and machined titanium and steel details pass through penetrant and magnetic particle lines before delivery. Eddy current techniques are approved by your eddy current Level 3; what we add is the record discipline around them, so that every technique names its reference standard, probe, instrument settings and the parts it covers, and every certified technician running it can be shown to hold eddy current at the right level. Penetrant and magnetic particle files get the same treatment against ASTM E1417 and ASTM E1444 and your customers' own specifications.

A first Nadcap NDT audit for a growing subtier shop

Unmanned-systems growth has pulled new companies into the aerospace supply chain, and some San Diego shops are preparing for their first Nadcap NDT accreditation rather than a renewal. The initial audit is the hardest one. Before the auditor arrives, the supplier completes self-audits against AC7114 and the slash sheets for each process it is seeking, and those self-audits must reflect the shop as it really operates, with objective evidence ready for each answer. Weak self-audits, answered from the checklist rather than from the records, are a common reason initial audits run long and end with many findings.

For a first audit we work through the self-audit questions with your team one at a time, point to the record that answers each, and list everything that does not yet exist. That list usually includes a written practice that has never been audited against NAS 410, examinations that were never formally blueprinted, process control logs started recently, and a records procedure that does not mention NDT at all. We draft those items for approval, run a mock audit once they are in use, and help schedule the work so the new records have some history behind them by audit day. The NDT audit consulting page describes the readiness steps in more general terms.

Reference standards built in-house

Composite reference standards are often fabricated by the supplier itself, with inserts or flat-bottom features placed at known depths in a laminate built like the production part. Auditors treat these standards as measuring equipment. They expect a drawing or specification for each standard, a fabrication record showing materials and layup, a verification record confirming the flaws are where the drawing says, a unique identification marked on the standard, and a periodic condition check. A standard that exists only as a panel on a shelf with a handwritten label will draw a finding no matter how good the inspection technique is.

We set up a reference standard register with those fields, prepare a verification record template your Level 3 can sign, and link each standard to the techniques that use it. Metallic reference blocks for penetrant, magnetic particle and ultrasonic work go into the same register, along with their certifications. For the wider documentation picture, see Level III documentation services.

Shops that work for both the airfield and the waterfront

San Diego is also a major naval shipbuilding and ship repair port, and some local NDT providers and fabricators serve both aircraft programs and ship work. Naval ship work runs on NAVSEA's own NDT requirements, while aircraft and aerospace hardware follows NAS 410 or whatever the aviation contract invokes. A technician may hold certifications under both schemes, but the records must be kept so that an auditor from either side can find the right certification, the right examinations and the right procedures without confusion.

We help dual-program shops separate the two cleanly: distinct certification records, examinations filed by scheme, procedures that cite the governing document correctly, and a cross-reference showing which personnel hold which scheme in which method. Depot-related work deserves a careful read of the contract, too, because work done by or for the government depot follows Navy maintenance and inspection requirements that the contract will spell out. If your shop's main exposure is the waterfront, our maritime NDT consulting in San Diego page covers that side.

Defense data, ITAR and examination banks

Specific examinations under NAS 410 test the procedures, specifications and acceptance criteria a technician actually uses. In a defense supply chain, those documents frequently include export-controlled technical data, which means the examination questions built from them are controlled too. Auditors will ask how the examination bank is protected from compromise, and an ITAR-registered company has its own reasons to know where those files live and who can see them.

When we review or redesign examination files for San Diego clients, the controlled content stays where you keep it. We agree at the start which files we may receive, which we review on your premises, and which we review over a session you host. Templates, blueprints and question-writing guidance can be prepared outside your systems because they contain no controlled data; the questions themselves are written or finalized inside them by your examiners.

What our gap review covers

  • The written practice measured against NAS 410, plus EN 4179 for programs with European customers, including outside agencies, interrupted service, examination rules and records retention.
  • The Responsible Level 3 designation and the arrangement for methods outside that person's certifications.
  • Personnel files for a sample of technicians in each method: training, experience, the three examinations, vision, certification and recertification.
  • Procedures and technique sheets for approval, revision control and flow-down of each prime specification.
  • Reference standards, instrument calibration and process control logs.
  • Subcontracted NDT: how each provider is approved, monitored and reviewed. Our subcontractor approval audit page explains the controls auditors expect.

The output is a findings list ranked by audit risk, followed by drafted corrections marked for approval. Procedures can be managed afterward in a controlled register such as the procedures app, which keeps approved revisions locked.

Revision 6: deciding on the points route

NAS 410 Revision 6 dates from December 2025. Its most discussed addition, Appendix D, gives Level 2 personnel a path to the initial Level 3 examination by earning points for designated NDT activities, and AIA describes the revision as clarifying certification requirements more broadly. For an unmanned-systems supplier growing its own senior inspectors, the points route may be attractive, but only if activity records exist that a Level 3 can verify. We redline your written practice against the new revision, set out the decision on Appendix D for your Level 3, and draft a points log if you adopt it. Background is in NAS 410 explained and the comparison in NAS 410 versus SNT-TC-1A.

Working with Atlantis from San Diego

An engagement usually starts with a scope call and a document review done remotely, then a site visit to your San Diego facility for a mock audit in which we pull files from the floor and watch a job run against its approved technique. After a real audit, we help with root-cause analysis and the objective evidence needed to close findings. Bring the written practice, your certified personnel roster, the prime specifications and contract quality clauses you work to, and your most recent audit report.

Related pages: aerospace NDT in San Diego, NDT training in San Diego (ASNT SNT-TC-1A based; under NAS 410 your Responsible Level 3 decides whether outside hours count), what a Responsible Level 3 does, and the national overview of NAS 410 audit compliance documentation.

faq.q: Can a consultant hold the Responsible Level 3 designation for a San Diego supplier?
faq.a: NAS 410 allows an outside agency to provide Level 3 services where the employer chooses and the customer accepts, but Atlantis does not take that designation. Our drafts and reviews go to your own Responsible Level 3, who approves them, while your company stays the certifying employer.

faq.q: Our ultrasonic scan program was adjusted on the machine. Do we need to revise the technique sheet?
faq.a: Yes, if the change affects any parameter the technique sheet controls. An auditor comparing the approved sheet with the loaded program will treat a mismatch as an unapproved technique. Revise the sheet, have your ultrasonic Level 3 approve it, and record why the change was made.

faq.q: How should we document composite reference standards we make ourselves?
faq.a: Treat each as measuring equipment: a drawing or specification, a fabrication record, a verification record of flaw locations, a unique marking and periodic condition checks, all linked to the techniques that use it. We can set up that register and its templates.

faq.q: We do NDT for both naval ships and aircraft. Can one written practice cover both?
faq.a: Usually not cleanly, because naval ship work follows NAVSEA requirements while aircraft work follows NAS 410 or the aviation contract. Keep separate certification records and examinations for each scheme, with a cross-reference of who holds what. See our San Diego maritime consulting page for the ship side.

faq.q: Does Atlantis train or examine technicians for NAS 410?
faq.a: No. Atlantis does not deliver NAS 410 training or examinations and does not certify personnel to NAS 410. We help your program's own examiners with templates and blueprints, and help your Responsible Level 3 keep examination records audit-ready.

faq.q: How do you handle export-controlled technique sheets and examination questions?
faq.a: We agree the handling at the outset: controlled files are reviewed at your facility or in a session you host, and never stored on our systems unless you authorize it. Templates and guidance without controlled content can be prepared remotely.

faq.q: Our prime customer audits us in addition to Nadcap. What is different about its audit?
faq.a: A prime's own audit checks compliance with its specifications and flow-downs, which often go further than NAS 410 on technique approval, reporting and customer-specific training. Build a customer requirements matrix so you can show where each requirement is met.

faq.q: Is the mock audit done at our site or remotely?
faq.a: At your site. Floor observation and random file pulls need someone physically present, so the mock audit normally happens at your San Diego facility, with document work handled remotely. Our people come from the Houston and Hyderabad offices for that visit.

faq.q: What should we send to get started?
faq.a: Your written practice, certified personnel roster with methods and levels, the prime specifications and contract quality clauses you work to, and your latest audit report. Send a summary through the contact form.
